name: Abaloparatide
route: Daily injection under the skin from a prefilled pen
status: FDA-approved for osteoporosis at high fracture risk in postmenopausal women and in men
mechanism: Activates the parathyroid hormone receptor on bone-forming cells to build new bone instead of only slowing bone loss
uses: Postmenopausal osteoporosis at high fracture risk
Osteoporosis in men at high fracture risk

article.summary: Abaloparatide (Tymlos) is a daily bone-building injection for people with osteoporosis at high fracture risk. It sharply cut new spine fractures in postmenopausal women in a major trial.
article.takeaway: Abaloparatide is a lab-made analog of PTHrP, a natural protein related to parathyroid hormone that signals bone-building cells. In the ACTIVE trial, new spine fractures occurred in 0.6% of women on abaloparatide and 4.2% on placebo over 18 months.[^1][^2] Unlike most osteoporosis drugs, which slow bone loss, it adds new bone. The label limits use to 2 years over a lifetime, and common side effects include high urine calcium and dizziness.[^1]
glance: Approved (Tymlos) for postmenopausal women and for men with osteoporosis at high fracture risk[^1]
Reducing fractures in postmenopausal osteoporosis; raising bone density in men
Daily injection under the skin with a prefilled pen, for no more than 2 years in a lifetime[^1]
ACTIVE (2,463 women), its extension, and ATOM (228 men)

blocks.text: Most osteoporosis drugs, such as bisphosphonates, slow the cells that break bone down. Abaloparatide works the other way. It is an analog of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) that activates the same receptor as parathyroid hormone and switches on bone-forming cells.[^1] Given once a day, it produces short pulses of signal that favor new bone over breakdown.

items: **Postmenopausal women** with osteoporosis at high fracture risk, or who failed or could not tolerate other treatments; it reduces spine and non-spine fractures[^1]
**Men** with osteoporosis at high fracture risk, to increase bone density[^1]

rows: New spine fractures 0.6% vs 4.2% on placebo at 18 months[^1][^2]
With 24 more months of alendronate, spine fractures 0.9% vs 5.6% over 43 months[^3]
Lumbar spine bone density up 8.5% vs 1.2% on placebo at 12 months[^4]

blocks.text: In ACTIVE, high blood calcium was less common with abaloparatide (3.4%) than with open-label teriparatide (6.4%).[^2] The trial in men measured bone density, not fractures.

Tymlos comes as a prefilled pen that delivers 30 daily doses of 80 micrograms. It is injected under the skin of the abdomen once a day. The label says safety and effectiveness have not been studied beyond 2 years, and use for more than 2 years during a lifetime is not recommended.[^1] A drug that holds the gains, such as alendronate, usually follows.[^3]

items: **Common in women:** high calcium in urine, dizziness, nausea, headache, palpitations, fatigue, upper abdominal pain and vertigo[^1]
**Common in men:** injection-site redness, swelling and pain, dizziness, joint pain and nausea[^1]
**Blood pressure:** it can drop on standing after a dose; sit or lie down if dizzy[^1]
**Calcium:** avoid with existing high blood calcium; kidney stones and high urine calcium are possible[^1]
**Osteosarcoma:** rats given high exposures developed bone tumors; it is unknown whether humans would, and the current label has no boxed warning[^1]

blocks.text: It is avoided in people at higher baseline risk for bone cancer, including those with Paget's disease, bone metastases, prior skeletal radiation or open growth plates.[^1]

evidence.label: Strong: large randomized fracture trial
evidence.text: ACTIVE enrolled 2,463 women and measured fractures directly.[^2] Evidence in men is limited to bone density rather than fractures.[^4]

faq.q: How is abaloparatide different from teriparatide?
faq.a: Both build bone. [Teriparatide](/peptides/teriparatide) copies the first 34 amino acids of parathyroid hormone, while abaloparatide copies PTHrP. In ACTIVE, high blood calcium was less frequent with abaloparatide, though teriparatide was given open-label.[^2]

faq.q: How long can it be used?
faq.a: The label advises against more than 2 years in a lifetime.[^1] A bone-protecting drug is usually used afterward, as studied in ACTIVExtend.[^3]
It is approved to raise bone density in men with osteoporosis. In ATOM, spine bone density rose 8.5% vs 1.2% on placebo over 12 months.[^4]
